To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mucins isolated from sputa from patients with chronic bronchitic disease contain basic proteins (mucus proteinase inhibitor, lysozyme) which interact with the carbohydrate chains of the mucins.
mucins from human bronchial sputum contain basic proteins such as mucus proteinase-inhibitor (MPI) and Lysozyme (LZ).
mucins isolated from sputa of a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) contain mucus proteinase inhibitors (MPI) and Lysozyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interactions between basic proteins and the carbohydrate chains of glycoproteins in the large airways of patients with chronic bronchial disease.

the study of interactions between mucins (glycoproteins secreted by the goblet cells of the bronchial epithelium) and two basic proteins (mucus proteinase inhibitor [MPI] and lysozymes [LSZ]) in the secretions from the large airways of patients suffering from chronic bronchitis
the study of the structure and functions of the glycoproteins (mucins) of human bronchial mucous secretions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mucins of the large airway secretions are not free but are associated with other proteins such as MPI and LSZ, and that these associations are due to strong ionic interactions between acidic residues of the carbohydrate chain of mucins and basic residues of these proteins.
mucins and proteins in the mucus gel are in a dynamic equilibrium.

the interactions between mucins, MPI and LSZ are strong enough to be detected in vitro, and are not destroyed by the isolation procedure, but that these interactions are not strong enough to prevent the separation of the components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the basic proteins MPI and LSZ, in the presence of high salt concentrations, are able to bind to the mucins in human bronchitis secretions.
mucins are the major components of bronchial mucus, which is a gel formed by a network of cross-linked glycoprotein molecules.

the ionic interactions between mucus proteinase inhibitory and lysozymes and the mucin glycoproteins of the large airway secretions could be a factor in the protection of the mucins against proteolytic attack and in the maintenance of the rheological properties of mucus in disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mucins isolated from the sputum from the chronic bronchitis patient were able to bind to the basic proteins MPI and LSZ.
the mucins isolated from sputa from a patient with a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease were still associated with two basic proteins, the mucus proteinase (MUC) and lysozome.
the interactions between mucins, MPI and LSZ are strong enough to be maintained during mucin preparation procedures, and that they can be disrupted by increasing the ionic strength of the medium.
